title: Firmware watchdog and soft-reset noise: nightshift investigation notes
content:
Summary:

Nightshift observed a cluster of intermittent soft-resets and firmware watchdog timeouts across 3 racks (rack-a12, rack-a13, rack-b02) between 2027-03-12 23:30 and 2027-03-14 04:10 UTC. Symptoms: short-lived job failures (OOM/restart), nvidia driver recovering messages in dmesg, and transient NVLINK re-negotiation logs. Node-level watchdog messages precede GPU resets by ~2-20s. ECC correctable counts spike in minutes leading up to a reset in two of the three nodes.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture nightshift timeline and raw evidence for triage.
- Propose an interim oncall mitigation checklist (quick triage/runbook) to reduce customer impact.
- List hypotheses and next steps for lab validation and vendor escalation.

High-level findings (quick):
- Pattern: firmware watchdog timeout -> kernel logs: "firmware watchdog expired for GPU X" -> driver recovery (Xid 13/31-like) -> NVLINK reinitialize messages.
- ECC: Correctable ECC counts increase in the 5–15 minute window before reset on two nodes; one node had no ECC pattern but showed a persistent PCIe link flapping entry.
- Driver versions: incidents primarily hit nodes on nvidia-driver 555.34-stable; a smaller set on 545.20. Select nodes with 560.10 are not impacted (low sample size).
- Power/thermal: no sustained thermal run-ups; temperatures were nominal (< 78C).
- Workload correlation: long autoregressive decoding jobs (GPT-like) with large KV caches and >1024 token sequences had higher incidence.

Timeline (selected events):
- 2027-03-12 23:37 UTC — rack-a12/node-173: first watchdog timeout; jobs restarted by k8s; dmesg shows "GPU 0: firmware watchdog expired" then "NVRM: Xid 31" then "NVLINK: Link change detected".
- 2027-03-13 01:14 UTC — rack-a13/node-182: repeated short resets (3 in 40m). ECC correctable rose from 12 -> 412 in 9m before first reset.
- 2027-03-13 02:01 UTC — rack-b02/node-94: single reset, no ECC spike; dmesg shows "PCIe: Link Retrain" entries prior to driver hang.
- 2027-03-14 03:50 UTC — cluster-wide alert: aggregated job failure rate up 0.8% for hosted-api region-us-west-2.

Collected evidence (how we grabbed logs):
- node: node-173 (rack-a12)
  - journalctl -k --since "2027-03-12 23:30" > ~/evidence/node-173-kernel.log
  - sudo dmesg | tail -n 400 > ~/evidence/node-173-dmesg.log
  - nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,MEMORY,PCI > ~/evidence/node-173-nvidia-smi.txt
  - /var/log/powercap.log included a couple brief power capping events but timestamped earlier in the day.
- kube: pod logs for top 3 failed pods saved (hosted-api-*-decoder)
- perf traces: run perf on a lab replica when we can reproduce

Immediate oncall triage checklist (urgent steps for first responder):
1) Verify alert details and scope: query k8s by node label and failing pods.
   - kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> -o wide | grep CrashLoop or Error
2) SSH into node, collect quick evidence:
   - sudo dmesg | tail -n 200
   - sudo journalctl -k -n 500 --no-pager
   - nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,DRIVER,PCIE
3) If node shows "firmware watchdog expired" or Xid-like recoverable error:
   - cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
   - drain gracefully if >1 job impacted or repeated resets: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
   - capture full logs to /tmp/evidence-<node>-<ts> and attach to JIRA SRE-4182
4) Try soft recovery on the node:
   - sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
   - if modprobe fails or driver unload is refused, proceed to power-cycle the host (coordinate with datacenter ops)
5) If NVLINK negotiation appears noisy (repeated "link change" entries) attempt to disable NVLINK for the node as temporary mitigation (lab-only procedure — requires module/driver flags):
   - Note: disabling NVLINK reduces throughput for multi-GPU jobs — use only if stability outweighs perf.
6) Reintroduce to cluster only after 30m stable and observed no new ECC/timeout messages.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Firmware watchdog triggered by accumulation of correctable ECC errors leading to internal GPU microcontroller stall. Rationale: ECC spikes precede reset on two nodes.
B) NVLINK negotiation instability or PCIe retrain causing temporary I/O latency spike that trips firmware watchdog. Rationale: node-94 logs show PCIe link retrain; NVLINK log lines present.
C) Driver/firmware incompatibility with heavy KV cache workloads and long attention sequences; some driver versions more tolerant.
D) Power supply hiccups causing transient undervoltage detected by firmware (least likely given powercap logs, but not ruled out).

Longer-term follow-ups / action items (owners assigned):
- Asha/Kevin (SRE): Provision two lab nodes with same firmware/driver versions and synthetic KV long-sequence load to reproduce. Target by 2027-03-21.
- Miguel (Applied ML): Provide a trimmed workload that reproduces in <30m (reduce network and scheduler noise). Target 2027-03-18.
- Benji (Infra): Run subset of affected nodes on driver 560.10 in staging; compare ECC and watchdog events. Q2 gates: 2027-03-24.
- Eng-Platform: Create dashboard for "gpu.watchdog.count" and ECC correctable delta per 10m per node; add alert when delta > 200 in 10m. Goal: 2027-03-22.
- Escalation: if lab reproduces or upgrades don't mitigate, open vendor support case with NVIDIA, include nv-host engine logs and firmware diagnostics (SRE-4182).

Draft runbook excerpt (for inclusion in ops handbook):
- Detection: Alert when kernel log contains /firmware watchdog expired|NVRM: Xid/ or when gpu.watchdog.count increases by >1 in 5m.
- Prioritization: If more than 1 node per rack in same cluster shows resets within 6h or customer-impact >0.5% error rate, treat as Sev2 and assemble cross-team war room.
- Mitigation steps: follow Immediate oncall triage checklist above.
- Safe rollbacks: pin to driver 545.20 if 555.34 shows higher incidence while lab tests run — but require validation for perf regressions.

Diagnostics we still need:
- nv-host logs (user-space firmware comms) from affected nodes — currently only partially captured. Need to enable full debug on 2 suspect nodes during repro attempts.
- Telemetry: capture PCIe link state over time (+/- 1m granularity) and NVLINK error counts.
- Collect GPU micro-controller logs (if available) and firmware dump.

Notes from quick log snippets (redacted):
- "[ 2342.109831] gpu-wdt: firmware watchdog expired on GPU 0
  [ 2342.109832] NVRM: Xid 31: GPU:0: GPU exception on thread 0x2d"
- "[ 2430.712412] nvlink0: link change detected slot 1 -> renegotiate"
- "ECC correctable: 12 -> 412 (delta 400 over 9m)"

Risks and trade-offs:
- Disabling NVLINK or pinning drivers may reduce throughput and increase cost per token. But repeated resets cause job restarts and user-visible failures; short-term stability preferred.
- Aggressive cordon/drain reduces available capacity and may impact SLAs for low-redundancy customers. Communication with CS required for mid-sized incidents.

Open questions for engineering/firmware teams:
- Does the GPU firmware expose ECC thresholds that trigger watchdogs?
- What is the safe procedure to capture a firmware dump non-invasively?
- Could our autoscaler/packer be scheduling too many long-KV jobs onto contiguous NVLINK topologies, amplifying failure cascade?

Attachments / evidence pointers: see linked_artifacts (JIRA SRE-4182) and attached logs in the JIRA ticket: node-173-dmesg.log, node-182-ecc-trace.csv, node-94-pcie-trace.txt.

Immediate recommendation for next 72 hours:
- Add temporary alert for ECC-correctable-delta > 200 in 10m per node.
- Start controlled driver rollout on a small canary subset (Benji to run 5 nodes) to 560.10 and measure watchdog/Xid occurrences vs 555.34 baseline.
- Prioritize repro in lab with Miguel's synthetic workload.

If you are the responder reading this at night: follow the oncall checklist, attach logs to SRE-4182, ping @miguel and @benji on slack for quick coordination, and escalate to oncall lead if more than 2 nodes in a rack fail in a 2h window.

-- Asha (notes)
